name: Herod Antipas
bio: Herod the tetrarch (Herod Antipas), son of Herod the Great, imprisoned John the Baptist at the urging of his wife Herodias after John condemned their marriage, though he feared the crowds who honored John as a prophet and hesitated to kill him. At a birthday banquet, Herodias's daughter danced for him, and he rashly swore to grant her any request; prompted by her mother, she asked for John's head, and Herod reluctantly had him beheaded. When he later heard of Jesus's growing fame, he feared John had risen from the dead (Matthew 14:1-12). His later role in Jesus's trial is told in detail in the chapters ahead.
